title: Which Way
logline: On the back roads of the dry zone, with no signs and no signal, Chathura keeps stopping to ask the way. Every person points somewhere different, and every answer comes with a small piece of a life.

object.note: Object 4 (identity not chosen) could enter only if a stranger on the road genuinely gives or trades something. Never staged.

thread_in.thread: The question of which way to go leaves a family's evenings and becomes a real road: on unsigned dry-zone tracks, Chathura keeps stopping to ask the way.

thread_out.thread: Every answer on the road came from where the person stood; next, people whose own map no longer matches the ground walk out across a drained reservoir looking for where home was.

requirements: A real destination reached by poorly signed rural roads
Low mobile coverage along the route
Freedom to stop and film brief encounters with consent

suggestions.why: A large, thinly populated dry-zone district with many minor roads between villages and tanks.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Not knowing which way to go is not a failing in itself. But when the mind cannot settle on anything, the texts say it feels neither good nor bad, just flat and stalled.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: යන්නේ කොහේද කියා නොදැන සිටීම වරදක් නොවේ; නමුත් තීරණයකට එන්න බැරිව හිත පැටලී සිටින විට එය සතුටකුත් නැති, දුකකුත් නැති හිස් ගතියක් ලෙස දැනේ.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma describes doubt (vicikicchā) as the state of a mind so clouded by delusion that it cannot come to a decision about its object. Because such a mind never properly grasps what is in front of it, it can neither enjoy nor dislike it, so it always comes with neutral feeling. The texts are careful to separate this from ordinary uncertainty about something not yet known, which Pradeepika calls look-alike doubt and says may not be unwholesome at all.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Junction after junction, the vehicle slows, stops and turns back, and every stranger points a different way from where they stand. The low, looping stretches between answers carry the flat, unlanded feeling, while the warmth of the people who stop to help shows that asking is not the problem. The film lets the moment a road is finally chosen arrive without comment.

key_terms.en: doubt; inability to reach a decision
accompanied by neutral feeling (here a dull flatness, not calm)
look-alike doubt: ordinary uncertainty about something unknown

lesson.caution: This is not an argument against questioning: the texts say honest not-knowing is not the harmful doubt, and the people giving directions are not shown as confused or foolish.
lesson.builds_on: Group 3 ended as the heat of anger faded and left confusion behind; this first film of the new stage shows what that confusion feels like: not pain, but a grey inability to settle.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
